title: Depth-three circuits beyond the square root
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's theorem (2026) that one explicit language, decidable in polynomial time, needs depth-three OR-AND-OR circuits with more than 2^(A sqrt n) gates for every constant A at every large length: a restriction bound that writes a restricted CNF of width k as a signed combination of CNFs of constant width with bounded expected weight, whatever the number of clauses; a partition of a CNF of bounded width into few sparse CNFs with disjoint supports, by sunflowers; a language that evaluates a polynomial at a linear hash, whose random slices have limited independence on small subcubes; and a count of all gates of a circuit.
prerequisites: finite probability: expectation, independence, Markov's inequality, the union bound
the existence of a field with 2^r elements (core course Abstract Algebra II, Judson, Theorem 22.1.6) and division with remainder for polynomials over a field
the course proves every other fact it uses

checks.exact_checks: Python (scratch dt_checks.py, 11 Oct 2026), exact arithmetic and exhaustive enumeration: 95795 checks of 56 kinds, 0 problems. Restricted CNFs (random CNFs on 2 to 6 variables, widths up to 4, b = 1 and 2): the finite expansion pointwise on every live cube; path lengths, distinct indices and the counts a_U >= c_U >= h; cylinders, constancy of c_U and the identity 'path term = weight times mixture'; the inequality |E G H| <= W corr_b(G) with corr_b computed over all CNFs of width b; E W <= 1/(1-theta) and E W_j <= theta^j summed exactly over all restrictions; the reweighting identity; the single-clause example. The marker mixture by listing all orders. Sunflowers: random families above the Erdős-Rado bound and the transversal family. The sparse partition procedure run on 362 random CNFs (widths up to 4, thresholds 2 and 3, up to 49 leaves, 1,683 branching steps): antichains, fresh insertions, the branching identity, the bound e_u + 1 for added clauses at every state, N_u <= D_u m, step and branch-1 budgets, occurrence and clause counts at leaves, the partition of H into disjoint leaves, and the leaf count against the entropy bound. The hash: uniformity of h(w) for every nonzero w (d up to 5). Finite fields: irreducible polynomials of degree 1 to 10, the degree count, R_P a field for an irreducible P and not for a reducible one. Interpolation: uniformity of the values at up to t points and independence of the signs, over the fields with 4 and 8 elements; the fourth moment with 4-wise independent signs. The parameters r, t and the block lengths for 3,341 values of d. Binomial tails of the live set. The arithmetic of the last lesson; for A = 1: B = 256, Q = 13312 and a sufficient width of about 36,000.

checks.source_reading: OpenAI preprint 'Beyond the Square-Root Exponent for Depth-Three Boolean Circuits' (23 Sep 2026), TeX read in full (introduction, preliminaries, restriction, sparse partition, construction, lower bound, appendix on finite fields; library copy openai-math-20261006); every step rederived; no error found. Lean scope document lean/docs/112.md read. Differences: the restriction bound is split into two lessons (the exact expansion; weights and backward counting) with worked small cases; the existence of a suitable modulus P is proved from the existence of a field with 2^r elements by counting elements of smaller degree, and the course only needs that R_P is a field; the sparse partition is proved with the survivors and the deletions counted separately; the last lesson states where the square root comes from and gives the size of the constants for A = 1.
